name: Paston
description: Paston is a highly localized and strategically deep trick-taking game played primarily in Armenia and the Armenian diaspora. Played by three players with a 32-card deck, it belongs to the family of games like Preferans and Belote. The game is known for its unique suit terminology (e.g., 'Paston' for Spades) and the 'Prikup' (two face-down cards given to the declarer). It is a game of skill, involving intense bidding for the right to name the trump suit and reach a target score of 121.

history.origins: Rooted in the interaction between Eastern European trick-taking traditions and Middle Eastern social gaming. It bears strong similarities to 'Pastushok' and 'Preferans'.
timeline: 1800s: Rules for Paston coalesce in the Caucasus region.
1920s: Becomes a standard social activity in Armenian 'Koffeehouses'.
1990s: Post-Soviet resurgence, with games appearing in professional social circles in Yerevan.
Present: A symbols of heritage for Armenians worldwide, often passed down through generations.
history.evolution: The game was simplified from 4rd-player variants to focus purely on the 3-player dynamic, which ensures every player is actively involved in every round.

setup.players: Three players; no partnerships. The game is played mainly in Armenia (e.g. Gyumri). Deal, bidding and play are clockwise; each player plays for themselves toward 121 points.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 10 cards (often dealt 2 at a time). 2 cards are placed face-down in the 'Prikup'.

rules.objective: Be the first player to reach 121 cumulative points.
rules.gameplay: Deal 10 cards to each player and 2 face-down to the prikup. Players bid by passing or naming a trump suit (Paston, Glitch, Dineri, Gupa, Paston grkha). Highest bidder becomes declarer, takes the prikup, discards two cards, and names trump. Declarer must take at least six tricks. Opponents may say whist (defend) or pass. Play: declarer leads; follow suit if possible, otherwise play a trump. Highest trump or highest card of led suit wins the trick; winner leads next. Scores are cumulative; game ends at 121 points.
keyRules: Follow suit if possible; if void, must play a trump.
Declarer must take at least six tricks or scores penalty.
Trump ranking: Paston (spades) lowest, then Glitch, Dineri, Gupa, Paston grkha (best spades) highest.
When all pass in bidding, holder of Jack of spades (or 7 of spades if Jack in prikup) becomes declarer.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Prikup! If you have a solid hand with 4 trumps, bid to get the extra 2 cards. Those 2 cards can fix a weak suit or give you the Ace you need to win your 6th trick. Don't be too aggressive without the Jack of your suit; the Jack is a powerful tool for 'Drawing' opponent trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Paston Grkha' (No-Trump) Risk: Only bid Grkha if you have Aces and Kings across at least three suits. Since there is no trump to save you, one long suit held by an opponent can destroy your contract. Conversely, if you are defending against a Grkha bid, try to figure out which suit the declarer discarded and lead precisely that suit.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Coordination: Like in Preferans, the two defenders should play 'Against the Declarer'. If your partner leads a suit, and you have the King while the Declarer has the Ace, play low to force the Ace out. Your goal is to make the Declarer use their power cards for small tricks, leaving them vulnerable to your 'Long Suit' in the final 4 tricks.
tips: The 7 of Spades is a 'Redeal' card in many Armenian circlesâ€”check your local house rules!
If you win only 5 tricks, you lose the 10 points. 6 is the magic number.

variations.name: Score when declarer surrenders
variations.description: In some rules opponents do not score 2 points when the declarer surrenders; in others they do. Affects whether sacrifice bids are more attractive.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring variant; no engine overrides documented in source.

variations.name: Paston grkha (best spades)
variations.description: Highest bid; spades are trump but with higher penalty for losing. Declarer scores only +10 for six tricks (not multiplied by 4); other scores multiplied by 4.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Best-spades bid variant; no engine overrides documented in source.

variations.name: Redeal conditions
variations.description: If bottom card is 7 of spades, cards are reshuffled and redealt. If a player holds 7-8-9-10-J-Q of spades but neither K nor A of spades, cards are shown and redealt by same dealer.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Redeal rules; no engine overrides documented in source.

scoring.description: Cumulative points per round; declarer scores +10 for six or more tricks, -10 for five or fewer; defenders score by tricks taken; multipliers apply for non-spade trumps.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 121 cumulative points wins.
